note.after_visit_summary: Today we looked at a mole on your left upper back that has changed in size and color. It showed some unusual features, so we performed a shave biopsy to check it under the microscope. The area was numbed, and the mole was removed. You will have a shallow wound that should heal in one to two weeks. Keep the bandage on for 24 hours, then clean the area gently each day, apply petroleum jelly, and cover with a fresh bandage. Biopsy results will be ready in 7 to 10 days and will be available in your patient portal. We will call you either way. If the area becomes red, hot, swollen, or drains pus, please call us right away. To protect your skin, use broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 30 or higher every day on exposed skin, reapply every two hours when outside, and wear a wide-brimmed hat. Check your moles monthly. Because of your sunburn history and number of moles, we recommend a full skin check every year. Your follow-up visit is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27th to review the biopsy site and results. If you have any questions before then, please call the clinic.
